decisions.rationale: Prader-Willi syndrome names one specific disease with a single definition and no further categorization; the whole phrase is preferred as the minimum necessary span.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate §1 (Specific Disease); §5 (minimum necessary span)

decisions.rationale: PWS is the abbreviation defined as Prader-Willi syndrome and is annotated as its own separate mention.
'neurogenetic disease' describes a family of multiple genetic neurological diseases rather than one specific disease.
Infantile hypotonia is a clinical sign or symptom, not a disease name or a family of diseases.

decisions.rationale: Gonadal hypoplasia is a descriptive clinical finding (underdeveloped gonads) rather than a named disease, and abnormality-type terms are excluded.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate §1; What NOT to Annotate §4 (general terms)

decisions.rationale: Hyperphagia is a symptom (excessive eating) rather than a disease mention.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate §1; What NOT to Annotate §4 (general terms)

decisions.rationale: Obesity is a single, well-defined medical condition with no further categorization, so it is annotated as a Specific Disease.
PWS used as the subject of the sentence refers to Prader-Willi syndrome; duplicate mentions are each annotated.
PWS modifies the noun 'region' (PWS region), so it is used as a Modifier for another concept.
PWS modifies the noun phrase 'IC element' (PWS IC element), so it is a Modifier.
Standalone PWS in 'leads to PWS' functions as the name of the disease itself, not as a modifier.
PWS modifies the noun 'family' (PWS family), so it is used as a Modifier.
PWS modifies the noun phrase 'IC element' (PWS IC element), so it is a Modifier.
